sections.h2: How does property tax work in Clark County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
In Clark County the sheriff mails the bill around October 1, the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets the value it is based on, and the county clerk takes unpaid bills after April 15. The sheriff's office states plainly that it never assesses property: the bill is the PVA's assessed value multiplied by the rate for each taxing entity that covers the parcel, such as the state, county, school district and any special district.

The county is small and close to Lexington. It covers 255 square miles, Winchester is the county seat and the only incorporated city, and the county is part of the Lexington-Fayette metropolitan area. The 2020 census counted 36,972 residents, so the tax base is larger and more urban than the eastern Kentucky counties around it.

sections.h2: Where can I pay a Clark County property tax bill?
sections.html:
The Clark County Sheriff's Office takes payment by several routes, and its 2025 taxpayer notice laid them out. The sheriff's office is in the basement of the Governor James Clark Judicial Building in Winchester, and the phone number for questions is (859) 744-4390.

Ways to pay the Clark County sheriff, from the 2025 County Taxpayer's Notice
MethodDetails in the notice
By mailCheck or money order to 17 Cleveland Avenue, Winchester, KY 40391; the USPS postmark counts, private meters do not
Drop boxCheck or money order in the box off West Broadway, with the bill number, map number or address written on it
OnlineDebit, credit or Google Pay through the sheriff's website, with merchant fees
In personCheck, money order or cash; cards with fees; 8:00 am to 4:00 pm Monday to Friday
Bank counterA downtown bank branch on West Broadway takes checks and money orders for the exact amount, with the bill, and no cash

If a bill has not reached you by October 15, call the sheriff. A buyer or mortgage company that should pay it needs the bill forwarded right away.

sections.h2: What are the Clark County due dates and penalties?
sections.html:
They are the same dates every year, set by KRS 134.015 and printed in the sheriff's notice. Use them as a recurring calendar rather than a one-time list.

  • Through November 1: pay in full and take a 2 percent discount.
  • November 2 to December 31: pay the bill as printed.
  • January 1 to 31: a 5 percent penalty applies.
  • February 1 to April 15: a 10 percent penalty plus a 10 percent add-on.

Unpaid bills transfer to the county clerk at the close of business on April 15. The sheriff's notice warns that payments at the clerk's office carry a 20 percent county attorney fee, a 10 percent clerk fee and interest at 1 percent per month, and that delinquent bills can be sold to a third party. The county's own FAQ says the same: bills go out October 1, the face amount ends December 31, and collection passes to the clerk after April 15.

sections.h2: What is Clark County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Clark County is an old settlement with a mix of in-town houses and farms. European settlement dates to about 1753, and the county was created in 1792 from Bourbon and Fayette counties. Railroads reached it in the 1870s and 1880s, and the later junction of I-64 and the Mountain Parkway near Winchester pulled manufacturing into the county in the 1950s and 1960s.

The 2020 census counted 14,917 households and 16,116 housing units, with 65.6 percent of occupied homes owned and 34.4 percent rented. Vacancy was 7.4 percent, and 71 percent of residents lived in urban areas. The median age was 41.5.

  • The Kentucky River, Red River, Lulbegrud Creek and Boone's Creek run through the county, so parcels near the water deserve a look at flood risk before you list.
  • Tobacco and livestock remain farm products in the county's rolling terrain.
  • Winchester holds an annual Beer Cheese Festival, and the dish originated in the county.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Clark County property assessment?
sections.html:
Call the Clark County PVA at (859) 745-0250 and ask for a conference before the roll inspection ends. Kentucky opens the roll for 13 days beginning the first Monday in May, and a conference is the required first step. A telephone conference is allowed if you request it.

If you still disagree, file a written appeal with the county clerk by the end of the next workday after inspection closes. Include the parcel, your reasons and your estimate of fair cash value. The board of assessment appeals then meets 25 to 35 days after the inspection period. You must support the appeal with facts such as sales listings, construction costs or loan documents.

The county judge/executive, a mayor or a school superintendent can also ask the board in writing to review specific assessments, which is how some values go up without an owner appealing. Still, you can keep the timeline simple: confer, file, bring comparable sales and pay on the value you claim.

sections.h2: How does the homestead exemption work in Clark County?
sections.html:
An owner who is 65 or older, or totally disabled, can have a fixed amount removed from the home's assessed value. The state figure is $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, and a new amount is published every two years. A house assessed at $210,000 would be taxed as if it were worth $160,900.

You file with the Clark County PVA. Age can be shown with a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. Disability claims need a federal or retirement system classification, and most must be renewed each year.

sections.h2: What if I sell a Clark County house with unpaid tax?
sections.html:
The balance is paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Ask the sheriff for the amount due on the current bill, and ask the county clerk whether any earlier bill became a certificate of delinquency. A lien from an unpaid year stays attached to the land for eleven years under KRS 134.015, regardless of who owns it, so a buyer's title company will find it.

The cheapest time to clear a balance is before April 15, when the sheriff holds the bill and fees are limited to the penalty and add-on. After that, the clerk's percentages stack on top, and a sale to an outside buyer is possible. If the house is vacant, inherited or needs repairs, an as-is buyer can pay the tax from your proceeds and close without you spending cash on repairs first.

Closing is also the moment to confirm who pays a bill that is still in the seller's name. Ask your closing agent to split the current year based on the date the deed transfers.

faqs.q: What number do I call about a Clark County tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the sheriff's office at (859) 744-4390 for bill and payment questions. For value questions call the Clark County PVA at (859) 745-0250.

faqs.q: When do Clark County tax bills go out?
faqs.a: Around October 1 each year. The 2025 notice said bills would be mailed on September 30 and posted online, and owners without a bill by October 15 should call.

faqs.q: Does the Clark County sheriff accept cash?
faqs.a: Yes, at the sheriff's office counter in Winchester. The downtown bank location listed in the 2025 notice does not accept cash.

faqs.q: Who sets the value of my Clark County home for tax?
faqs.a: The Clark County PVA, not the sheriff. The sheriff only collects the bill that results from the PVA's assessment and the local tax rates.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss April 15 in Clark County?
faqs.a: The unpaid bill moves to the county clerk, where fees of 20 percent for the county attorney and 10 percent for the clerk apply, plus 1 percent interest per month. It can also be sold to a third party.
